question: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and did something about it.

While testing a checkout flow I noticed users kept abandoning at the address step because the form didn't support PO boxes. I flagged it in our daily standup, built a quick prototype fix, and tested it with three customers who confirmed it worked.
What happened after you shared the prototype?
My manager had me pair with the backend person to ship it. Conversion on that step went up 8% the next month.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: New grad on payments team; noticed PO box rejection in checkout.
Action: Built prototype, tested with 3 users, raised in standup, paired to ship.
Outcome: 8% lift on step; shipped in two weeks.
Quote: "I just assumed we should support PO boxes like every other site."
Follow-up: Asked what happened after prototype; candidate described pairing and metric.
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the junior level. The candidate noticed a specific friction point during their own testing work, took initiative to prototype without being asked, and followed through by pairing to ship. Quote: "I just assumed we should support PO boxes like every other site." This shows ownership of their immediate scope and willingness to validate with real users. The 8% lift is modest but directly tied to their action. Biggest strength is closing the loop from observation to shipped change rather than stopping at a ticket.

lowerTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and did something about it.
Customers kept emailing support about the same feature request so I forwarded the tickets to the product manager.
Did you do anything else with the information?
Not really, that was the process we were told to follow.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: Support rotation; saw repeated feature requests.
Action: Forwarded tickets to PM.
Outcome: No further involvement or result mentioned.
Quote: "That was the process we were told to follow."
Follow-up: Asked if they did anything else; candidate stopped at ticket forwarding.
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the junior level. The candidate recognized a pattern in customer emails but took no ownership beyond routing the information per existing process. Quote: "That was the process we were told to follow." There is no evidence of digging deeper, validating the need, or attempting a small fix within their scope. The story ends with handoff rather than any outcome for customers. Biggest gap is treating customer signals as someone else's problem instead of showing initiative on work they already touch.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and acted on it.

Enterprise customers were manually exporting data to build weekly reports because our API lacked a batch endpoint. I ran usage queries, interviewed five customers, then worked with two other teams to design and launch the endpoint.
How did you get the other teams to prioritize it?
I brought the usage data and customer quotes to their planning meetings and showed the support ticket volume it would reduce.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: Senior backend engineer; saw manual reporting pain in enterprise.
Action: Queried usage, interviewed 5 customers, aligned two teams with data.
Outcome: Batch endpoint shipped; reduced support tickets.
Quote: "I brought the usage data and customer quotes to their planning meetings."
Follow-up: Asked how they influenced other teams; candidate described using data and ticket volume.
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the senior level. The candidate moved beyond their own service by analyzing usage data and conducting customer interviews to quantify the gap. Quote: "I brought the usage data and customer quotes to their planning meetings." They used concrete evidence to drive cross-team alignment without authority. The result was a shipped API change that addressed a real pain point. Biggest strength is combining customer insight with influence tactics to deliver measurable relief.

lowerTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and acted on it.
I saw a bunch of feature requests in the backlog for enterprise reporting so I added more detail to the existing ticket.
Did that change anything for customers?
Not yet, the ticket is still open.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: Senior engineer; noticed reporting requests in backlog.
Action: Added detail to an existing ticket.
Outcome: Ticket remains open; no customer impact.
Quote: "The ticket is still open."
Follow-up: Asked if anything changed for customers; candidate had no outcome.
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the senior level. The candidate identified a known gap but limited their action to updating a ticket rather than driving resolution. Quote: "The ticket is still open." There is no evidence of gathering data, talking to customers, or influencing prioritization across teams. The story shows awareness without the follow-through expected at this level. Biggest gap is staying within existing processes instead of creating leverage to close the need.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Our SMB segment was churning because onboarding took three weeks. I had my team shadow support calls, mapped the drop-off points, and restructured the onboarding flow with a new self-serve path.
How did you handle the team capacity?
I traded off two roadmap items and had the team present the churn data to get buy-in from leadership.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: Engineering manager; SMB churn tied to long onboarding.
Action: Had team shadow calls, mapped issues, traded roadmap items for new flow.
Outcome: Self-serve path launched; churn reduced.
Quote: "I traded off two roadmap items and had the team present the churn data."
Follow-up: Asked about capacity trade-offs; candidate described prioritization and leadership buy-in.
manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the manager level. The candidate used their team to diagnose a churn driver through direct customer touchpoints and then made explicit trade-offs to free capacity. Quote: "I traded off two roadmap items and had the team present the churn data." They turned customer insight into a shipped change while developing the team through the shadowing work. The outcome links team action to a business metric. Biggest strength is creating leverage by involving the team in both diagnosis and solution.

lowerTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and acted on it.
I saw high churn in the SMB segment so I asked the product team to look into it.
They continued on the existing roadmap while product investigated.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: Engineering manager; noticed SMB churn.
Action: Escalated to product team.
Outcome: No change to team work or customer experience.
Quote: "They continued on the existing roadmap while product investigated."
Follow-up: Asked what the team did; candidate kept team on prior priorities.
manager.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the manager level. The candidate recognized a business problem but delegated investigation entirely outside the team without adjusting their own priorities. Quote: "They continued on the existing roadmap while product investigated." There is no evidence of using the team to gather insight or making trade-offs to address the need. The story shows escalation without ownership of team outcomes. Biggest gap is failing to create leverage inside their own organization.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time you spotted an unmet customer need and acted on it.

We were losing large deals because procurement teams needed SOC2 and ISO certifications we didn't have. I sponsored a cross-org program, hired the first compliance lead, and shifted 15% of engineering capacity for nine months to close the gap.
We unlocked a new segment that now represents 22% of new ARR and the compliance team became a permanent function.

raiseNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.
Role: VP Engineering; lost deals due to missing certifications.
Action: Sponsored program, hired lead, reallocated 15% capacity for 9 months.
Outcome: New segment = 22% ARR; permanent compliance function.
Quote: "I sponsored a cross-org program... shifted 15% of engineering capacity."
Follow-up: Asked about long-term effect; candidate tied to ARR and org change.
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the exec level. The candidate connected a pattern of lost deals to a missing capability and made a multi-quarter, org-level investment to close it. Quote: "I sponsored a cross-org program... shifted 15% of engineering capacity." They accepted short-term roadmap cost for long-term market access and institutionalized the solution. The 22% ARR impact shows strategic judgment on customer segments. Biggest strength is translating customer signals into sustained organizational change rather than one-off fixes.

We kept hearing from sales about missing certifications so I had compliance added to the next planning cycle.
It was deprioritized when other initiatives came up.

lowerNotes: Q: Describe a situation where you identified an unmet customer need and acted on it.

Outcome: Deprioritized; no change.
Quote: "It was deprioritized when other initiatives came up."

exec.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for Customer / Client Focus at the exec level. The candidate noted a recurring sales blocker but did not protect the required investment when competing priorities emerged. Quote: "It was deprioritized when other initiatives came up." There is no evidence of strategic trade-offs or sustained sponsorship to address the customer segment gap. The story ends with the need remaining unmet. Biggest gap is lack of long-term ownership when ambiguity and resource pressure increased.
